cases.customer_question: When can a Bluetooth end product qualify primarily through Multi-Design reuse without requiring RF PHY testing?
question_variants: Does a pre-qualified module avoid RF PHY testing?
When is RF PHY testing mandatory for Bluetooth qualification?
Can an End Product qualification reuse existing Bluetooth certifications?
What is the difference between module reuse and board-level SoC implementation?
Does using an external antenna trigger Bluetooth RF testing?
cases.actual_issue: The customer wanted a cost estimate for Bluetooth SIG End Product qualification, but the real qualification issue was determining whether the hardware architecture qualified for reuse-only registration support or required mandatory RF PHY testing due to RF implementation differences.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth qualification effort depends heavily on how the Bluetooth hardware is integrated. If the product uses a pre-qualified module with an integrated antenna or approved antenna connector and does not change standard Bluetooth functionality, much of the qualification can be reused. However, if the Bluetooth SoC is mounted directly on the product PCB or uses a custom external antenna configuration, new RF testing is generally required because the final radio performance can change.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that reuse-oriented qualification support was possible only if the SoC or module and Host stack were already qualified and the product added no standard Bluetooth profiles beyond the existing qualified implementation, or only added proprietary profiles. Under those conditions, qualification could proceed through a Multi-Design reference registration approach. However, products using direct SoC implementation on the product board or modules with external antennas required RF PHY testing, with the test scope depending on supported PHY modes such as 1M, 2M, or Coded PHY.
cases.decision_logic: The determining factor is whether the end product preserves the previously qualified Bluetooth RF implementation and standard Bluetooth functionality. Integrated qualified modules with unchanged RF conditions can leverage qualification reuse, while board-level SoC integration or antenna modifications create a new RF implementation that requires RF PHY validation.
cases.final_recommendation: Verify early whether the product uses a fully qualified module with unchanged antenna conditions and unchanged Bluetooth-compliant functionality. If not, plan for RF PHY testing and include the associated qualification scope in the project estimate.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly assuming reuse eligibility could result in missing mandatory RF PHY testing, leading to qualification rejection, retesting, project delays, and unplanned qualification costs. Misclassification of antenna or SoC integration type could also create inaccurate customer quotations and incomplete compliance planning.
